sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.6136 Of 2019
Order:

The petitionerd/A1 and A2 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.88 of 2018 of Koilakuntla Police Station, Kurnool District, which was registered against them for the offences under Sections 188, 273 of IPC and Secs.26, 30 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act, 2006).

2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 26.10.2018 at about 03:45 P.M., the complainant along with his staff on credible information proceeded to the Pan shop of A1 situated besides SBI ATM, State Bank Road, Koilakuntla, Kurnool District, where A1 tried to run away towards the market, on questioning, he revealed that he purchased the banned tobacco products from A2.

Later, the complainant seized the said banned tobacco products under a cover of panchanama, arrested the accused and he registered the same as a case in Crime No.88 of 2018 for the offences stated supra.

3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 & batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto filed on the report of the Sub-Inspector of Police of Koilakuntla Police Station.
Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners/A1 and A2 under Sections 188, 273 of IPC and Thippugaari Venkateswara Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 16 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126277461/
